title: What stops an OAuth mix-up
desc: Five candidate defences against mix-up, where the client sends the code to the attacker's token endpoint. Storing the issuer bound to each request and comparing it with iss on return (RFC 9207) is the defence. Distinct redirect URIs are a fallback only if other options are unavailable (RFC 9700). By the lesson's own reasoning from RFC 9700 4.4.1, an aud check on a returned token comes too late, exact redirect matching passes because the shared URI is the client's own, and PKCE is not a defence because the client sends its verifier to the attacker's token endpoint with the code.
